$comment: Single source of truth for the riso press's STOCKS — the sheets a job can be run on — and what the mono drum prints on each. Canvas and PDF renderers cannot read CSS custom properties, so riso-press.js carries a literal copy of this table (PAPER / INK) and tools/verify-day-colours.mjs fails the build if the two drift. `day` and `night` are the keys the themes map to; `white` is Print Studio's true-white sheet (canon.print.stock in day-colours.json). Order is a picker's display order, light to dark.

white.label: White
white.note: Print Studio's true-white sheet; its K is canon.print.ink

steel.label: Steel
steel.note: a dark-but-not-black stock — opaque physics, cream drum

night.label: Night
night.note: the Night surface — opaque physics (a screenprint), cream drum

$darkRule: A stock whose R+G+B sum is below 340 prints OPAQUE (a silkscreen, not a riso): each plate covers what is under it. Everything lighter is translucent ink the sheet shows through. Decided with the separation press, 21–22.09.26.
